title: A Nutritionist Investigates Persistent Bloating
script: Dr. Ratna: [thoughtful] Bimo, you mentioned the bloating gets worse in the evenings. Has anything else changed recently besides your work schedule?
Bimo: Not that I've noticed, though I'll admit I haven't paid much attention to what I actually eat lately.
Dr. Ratna: [carefully] That's fairly common. Most people can describe their symptoms in detail but struggle to recall what triggered them.
Bimo: So what would you recommend? I've read conflicting things online about cutting out entire food groups.
Dr. Ratna: [reflective] Rather than eliminating everything at once, I'd suggest removing one likely trigger, dairy, for instance, for two weeks and observing carefully.
Bimo: Isn't that a bit slow? A friend of mine went gluten-free overnight and swore it transformed her digestion instantly.
Dr. Ratna: [honestly] It might have, genuinely, but removing several things simultaneously makes it nearly impossible to identify which change actually mattered.
Bimo: That's fair. I suppose I was hoping for a quicker answer than methodically testing one variable at a time.
Dr. Ratna: [gently] Understandable, though the gut tends to reward patience far more reliably than it rewards drastic overnight changes.
Bimo: Two weeks without cheese sounds miserable, if I'm being completely honest with you.
Dr. Ratna: [calmly] Most people say exactly that, and most people survive it perfectly well, occasionally even feeling noticeably better by the end.
Bimo: And if dairy turns out not to be the problem, what happens then?
Dr. Ratna: [encouraging] Then we reintroduce it and move to the next likely culprit, gluten or excess sugar, following the same method.
Bimo: Could this actually be something more serious, something I should be more concerned about?
Dr. Ratna: [seriously] It's unlikely, given your other results, but if the elimination approach doesn't clarify things, we'll investigate further with proper testing.
Bimo: That's reassuring, actually. I think I expected you to say something far more alarming.
Dr. Ratna: Keep a simple food diary alongside this, noting symptoms honestly, even the embarrassing ones you might want to leave out.
Bimo: Noted, though I make no promises about how honest that diary will be on weekends.
Dr. Ratna: I'll take partial honesty over none at all. Let's review everything together in two weeks.
